newsitem.title: USA: Citgo says Texas fire out, restoring other units.
newsitem.headline: Citgo says Texas fire out, restoring other units.

text.p: The explosion and fire that damaged an alkylation unit at Citgo's Corpus Christi, Texas refinery ran out Tuesday evening and Citgo is now restoring other units near the stricken unit, officials said.
"We gave an all clear at 8:30 last night (2030 CST/0130 GMT)," a Corpus Christi Police official told Reuters Wednesday, noting that meant the fire was out.
Citgo officials meanwhile said other units that were undamaged but came off line due to power loss associated with the blast, would be back up within 24 hours.
"The units surrounding the alkylation unit are all being brought up today and probably should be fully operational within a 24 hour period," said Citgo spokesman Kent Young.
Young said the affected units include aromatic plants that make cumene, benzene/tolulene/xylene (btx), a "hydrar" that hydrogenates cyclohexene, a petchem feedstock, and a "udex" unit.
Young and another Citgo official said the cause of the explosion and blaze that started Monday night remained unknown, but that investigators were on the scene.
But some emergency officials said there was a suspicion that some liquified petroleum gas (lpg) leaked out and caught fire before spreading to the alkylation unit.
When informed of such speculation, Citgo's Young reaffirmed that the cause remained unknown.

He said the alkylation unit, which produces high quality gasoline blending components, can run at rates varying between 17,000 and 20,000 barrels per day (bpd) depending on commercial factors. The refinery can process about 130,000 bpd of crude, he said.
Citgo Petroleum Corp is the U.S. unit of state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela SA.
-- Oliver Ludwig, New York Energy Desk, 1 212 859 1620
